common.task: Produce an editable draw.io reference diagram for the case. Use the same supplied facts and exact graph; do not invent services or connections. Choose the layout yourself.
common.output: One uncompressed mxGraphModel with plain mxCells, 1600 by 1000 canvas, white background, Arial labels at least 14 canvas units. Native separate text/shapes/connectors, not a flattened screenshot. No HTML labels, external images or personal filesystem paths.
common.metadata: Use the supplied component IDs as vertex IDs with csaRole=component and the declared scope attribute. Scope boundary vertices use the supplied IDs, csaRole=boundary and boundaryKind matching kind. Edge source/target must reference canonical component IDs, with kind and intent from the contract. Root model csaMode=reference. This metadata is for identical scoring, not a styling prescription.
common.assets: Both conditions may use the same local official SVG catalogs under assets/foundry and assets/fabric, or neutral native symbols with honest labels. Do not fetch assets. Embed any selected SVG without modification.
common.review: The evaluator exports PNG and measures source/contract, browser text, connector clarity and actual image defects. Unsupported automatic routing is a coverage limitation, not itself proof of a visual defect. One equal feedback opportunity is available to each condition.
common.edit_task: After generation and review, rename the first listed component by appending ' v2' and move that component and all its descendants 20 canvas units right in a separate edit-test copy. The evaluator checks whether endpoints stay attached and whether new collisions appear. Do not pre-apply this edit to the first diagram.

foundry.title: Two Foundry use cases sharing models
facts: Two application-owned web apps call separate agents in two Foundry projects inside one Foundry resource. Projects are development/ownership scopes, not subnets or runtime proxy hops.
Both agents use shared resource-owned model deployments. Only the support agent uses a configured Azure AI Search tool. Search remains an independent resource.
This is a logical request view with public authenticated HTTPS assumed, not a private-network design. Responses return on request paths. Do not imply automatic authentication/RBAC.

fabric.title: Fabric batch prediction lifecycle
facts: Curated Delta data in a lakehouse feeds a training notebook and a separate batch scoring notebook. Training logs to an MLflow experiment; a selected run is registered as a Fabric ML model.
A human-approved pinned model version controls batch PREDICT scoring. This is not native automatic approval or online serving.
Scoring writes predictions to a Gold lakehouse. A semantic model uses Direct Lake on that data; a Power BI report consumes the semantic model.
Data science and analytics use separate workspaces. Cross-workspace access must be authorized. This is one deployment stage, not dev/test/prod promotion.
